answer: Seven years, one number, the same three towers every night. Cell-tower triangulation tenure demands exactly that: a phone number seen at the same towers for years. No forger can print such a trail; it accrues one night at a time, and the tide of the scheme is patience the attacker cannot buy. A second identity needs its own seven-year trail, a third needs another, so the beacon that counts is a calendar, not a document. The final juniper test is a question to the carrier - towers match or the number is refused before it can vote, grade, or claim.
